requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Prepare a budget reflecting your expected income (allowance, gifts, wages), expenses, and savings for a period of 13 consecutive weeks. (b) Compare expected income with expected expenses. (1) If expenses exceed budget income, determine steps to balance your budget. (2) If income exceeds budget expenses, state how you would use the excess money (new goal, savings). (c) Track and record your actual income, expenses, and savings for 13 consecutive weeks (the same 13-week period for which you budgeted). (You may use the forms provided in the Personal Management merit badge pamphlet, devise your own, or use a computer-generated version.) When complete, present the records showing the results to your counselor. (d) Compare your budget with your actual income and expenses to understand when your budget worked and when it did not work. With your counselor, discuss what you might do differently the next time.

List these in order of importance to you. (b) Make a seven-day calendar or schedule. Put in your set activities, such as school classes, sports practices or games, jobs or chores, and/or Scout or place of worship or club meetings, then plan when you will do all the tasks from your to-do list between your set activities. (c) Follow the one-week schedule you planned. Keep a daily diary or journal during each of the seven days of this week's activities, writing down when you completed each of the tasks on your to-do list compared to when you scheduled them. Discuss what you might do differently the next time.

pamphlet_excerpts: Project Undertake: For any project you undertake, includingeducation or vacation, a plan will help you gain a better understanding of what it will take toaccomplish it.
Say Organizing Camping: Let’s say you are organizing a camping tripfor your family.
How longwill the trip be: one day, overnight, or longer?.
Planning Involve Deciding: Planning will involve deciding where to go, how you will get there, and how long it will taketo travel there.
step_by_step_procedure: Probably Want Aplace: You probably will want to go to aplace where you can do these activities.
Youalso Determine Season: Youalso will need to determine the best season to goand, if possible, see what the long-range weatherforecast will be.
Equipment Probablywill Not: The equipment needed probablywill not include more than hiking or walkingshoes, maybe binoculars, and appropriate clothing.
However Camping Trip: However, a camping trip might include moreactivities, such as canoeing, rappelling, backpacking, bicycling, skiing, or collectingspecimens of rocks.

Experts Say Onaverage: Experts say that, onaverage, people go through 10 different positions and threedifferent careers during their working lives.
But Career Morethan: But a career should be morethan a way to make a living.
Ideally Emotionally: Ideally, it should be emotionally, spiritually, and intellectually satisfying as well.
step_by_step_procedure: Choosing Acareer Doing: Try choosing acareer that you are good at doing and one that you truly like.
Tough Work Position: It can be tough to work in a position that you do not like, evenif you are earning a lot of money.
Trying Decide Career: If you are still trying to decide what career you would like topursue, do not worry.
Career Decisions Not: Sometimes career decisions are not madeuntil college or later.
